skill.name: simple
skill.description: Guides concise brainstorming before creative, architectural, or behavioral changes. It helps users discover context, compare two approaches, choose a direction, and capture key decisions.
skill.summary: Concise brainstorming workflow for planning changes before implementation.
skill.author: roin-orca

content.value_statement: Fast design discussions can lose focus or skip key trade-offs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a concise brainstorming flow before implementation.
actual_capabilities: Guides discovery before feature design, component creation, or behavior changes.
Prompts the assistant to compare two practical approaches with trade-offs.
Requires explicit user approval before implementation work begins.
Limits repeated proposal rounds to keep planning focused.
Captures the chosen direction in chat or a relevant implementation comment.
limitations: It does not implement code by itself.
It does not replace detailed design documents for large programs.
It depends on accurate project context from the assistant and user.
It is not a security review or testing workflow.

use_cases.title: Plan a small feature
use_cases.description: Use the skill to clarify intent, compare options, and select a practical path before coding.

use_cases.title: Choose an architecture direction
use_cases.description: Use the flow to compare two designs and explain the trade-offs before changing shared systems.

use_cases.title: Shape a component change
use_cases.description: Use the process to align behavior, constraints, and implementation scope before editing UI components.

prompt_templates.title: Start a quick brainstorm
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the simple brainstorming skill for this change. Help me clarify the goal, compare two options, and choose a direction.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small task

prompt_templates.title: Compare implementation options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the simple brainstorming process to propose two implementation approaches. Include trade-offs, risks, and your recommended direction.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a component update
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to assess the existing component patterns, ask any needed questions, and recommend a focused update plan.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate an architecture change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the simple brainstorming workflow for this architecture change. Consider constraints, migration cost, reversibility, and expected impact.

output_examples.input: I need to add saved filters to a dashboard.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks focused questions, compares local storage with server-backed filters, and recommends the best path for the current product scope.

output_examples.input: We may replace a shared data-fetching helper.
output_examples.output: The assistant summarizes current constraints, presents two migration options, explains trade-offs, and waits for approval before editing files.

output_examples.input: I want a cleaner settings page layout.
output_examples.output: The assistant reviews existing patterns, proposes two layout directions, and captures the selected plan before implementation starts.

best_practices: Provide the goal, constraints, and any files that matter before asking for proposals.
Ask for two options when the direction is unclear.
Approve a direction explicitly before asking the assistant to implement it.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill when you already have a precise implementation request.
Do not turn every small fix into a long design discussion.
Do not skip review of risky changes after a direction is chosen.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides a short brainstorming process before implementation work begins.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It asks the assistant to wait for approval before implementation.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before creative, architectural, component, or behavior changes.

faq.question: How many options does it compare?
faq.answer: It asks the assistant to present two approaches with trade-offs.

faq.question: Can it replace a formal design document?
faq.answer: No. It is best for fast planning and focused decisions.
